subject: Throughput commitment & streaming handshake — next steps
messages:
From: Rob Keller <rob.keller@novaretail.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-28T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Throughput & streaming SLO questions after demo

Thanks for the demo earlier today — good conversation. I wanted to capture the questions my infra team asked so we can size the qualification run: 

- Can you confirm typical p50/p99 per-token latency targets for streaming responses vs non-streaming (first-token and steady-state)?
- For throughput: we expect a peak of ~500 requests/minute during marketing-driven spikes; sustained baseline around 250 rpm. What are recommended concurrency limits per session?
- Streaming: our UI renders partial tokens; we care about inter-token latency and end-to-end first-token latency.

I've attached our internal perf requirements doc with some numbers (novaretail-performance-requirements.pdf). Happy to send sample conversations if that helps.

Rob
Rob Keller
Head of Platform
Novaretail

Attachments: novaretail-performance-requirements.pdf (application/pdf, 98KB)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Rob Keller <rob.keller@novaretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-29T09:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput & streaming SLO questions after demo

Rob — thanks for the doc and the clear list. Quick recap from our side and a proposed benchmark handshake so we can run a reproducible qualification: 

Summary of what we heard on the call:
- Peak throughput: ~500 rpm; sustained ~250 rpm.
- Concurrency: you mentioned 40–80 simultaneous interactive sessions during campaigns.
- Streaming requirement: partial-token streaming for chat UI; need low inter-token latency and strong first-token visibility.

Proposed measurable SLOs for the benchmark (we can iterate):
- Streaming inter-token latency: p50 <120ms / p99 <350ms (per token after first token)
- First-token end-to-end: p50 <450ms / p99 <800ms
- Sustained throughput test: 30m at 250 rpm with <1% errors
- Spike/concurrency test: 10m at 500 rpm with concurrency ramp to 80 sessions

Benchmark plan & artifacts we will exchange:
1) Prompt / conversation sets (you can provide redacted samples; we can also seed from our demo prompts) — format: JSONL, each record = user messages + expected behavior.
2) Eval harness: Docker image + runbook (we provide a template: redwood-benchmark-template.jsonl).
3) Measurement definitions: exact events we log (first_token, last_token, per_token_latency, server_cpu/gpu) and how we compute p50/p99.
4) Repro steps & infra: test infra spec, test window, and who runs the client vs server.

Timelines we propose:
- You provide sample conversation sets and any dataset NDA by 2026-10-02.
- We provision a benchmark environment and share the runbook by 2026-10-04.
- Kickoff test run: 2026-10-06 through 2026-10-08 (flexible).

Can you confirm: a) that the SLO targets above match your expectations, and b) whether your sample conversations should be treated as ephemeral sessions (no KV cache) or persistent sessions (with KV caching across turns)?

Next steps (quick checkboxes):
- [ ] Novaretail sends sample JSONL + NDA indicator
- [ ] Redwood shares benchmark template + runbook
- [ ] Confirm kickoff meeting (proposed: 2026-10-05 10:00 AM PT)

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call to hammer out specifics.

—
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0123
tessa_morgan@redwood.com

Attachment references: redwood-benchmark-template.jsonl (text/jsonl, 12KB)

From: Sara Lin <sara.lin@novaretail.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Rob Keller <rob.keller@novaretail.com>
Date: 2026-09-29T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput & streaming SLO questions after demo

Tessa — thanks, this is helpful. A few clarifications from infra/security: 

- The numbers you proposed look reasonable. Confirming that the streaming inter-token goals are per-token at the server boundary (we will measure in-browser render + server delta).
- Conversation mix: ~80% short single-turn Q/A, ~20% multi-turn commerce flows (3–8 turns). We'll send a representative JSONL with 500 entries (redacted).
- Sessions: we prefer persistent sessions (KV cache allowed) for multi-turn flows — that matters for caching and latency.
- Fallback behavior: during the spike test, we want Redwood to exercise the model-fallback policy (if the primary model is overloaded, fall back to a lower-cost 8-bit quantized variant) so we can validate quality vs latency tradeoffs.
- Data retention: session transcripts retained for 30 days; please confirm any logs you need to keep for reproducibility.

Attachments included: sample-conversation-sets.jsonl (text/jsonl, 76KB), sla-qos.png (image/png, 34KB). We can sign a short data-sharing NDA if required — Rob will route that.

Sara Lin
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Novaretail

2) Benchmark week locked: 2026-10-06 to 2026-10-08. Kickoff prep call: 2026-10-05 10:00 AM PT (30m) — calendar invite to follow.

3) What Redwood will deliver before the run:
- Dockerized eval harness + runbook (link below)
- Measurement spec (exact field names and aggregation script)
- Test infra spec and ephemeral credentials for the test client
- Commitment sheet to capture agreed SLOs and acceptance criteria (attached: NR-benchmark-commitment-sheet.pdf)

4) Key operational asks from Novaretail:
- Provide the sample JSONL by 2026-10-02 and indicate whether redaction is complete.
- Confirm whether KV caching is allowed for the multi-turn flows (Sara indicated yes).
- Confirm the fallback policy you'd like exercised (primary -> quantized fallback).

Links:
- HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/NR-2026-0930

If that all looks good, we'll send the kick-off invite and the runbook this afternoon.

Thanks — looking forward to running this with you.

—
Tessa Morgan
